notes: Merged from two passes that agree on the nine shared requirements (case 504 to critical, reopen_count 1, group 18 with assignee 803, user 803, membership 960, the two critical SLAs by natural key, link 216 removed, article 370 linked as 528) and on twelve of fourteen dispositions. disagreement: the reopened state: A in_progress, B IN ('new', 'in_progress'); kept in_progress as the benchmark's prior (logged in the requirement), so update_case is kept (A kept, B repaired). disagreement: the new user's cells: A email LIKE and role agent, B no email and role IN ('agent', 'manager'); kept the benchmark's exact email and role agent as the prior where nothing contradicts them (logged in the requirement). disagreement: the new user's location: both passes dropped it; set to 96 by the acting-user rule, which substitutes input.json's user into the benchmark's current-user premise instead of discarding the cell (logged in the requirement; the resolution least sure of). disagreement: owner_id of article 370: A 96, B none; kept 96 by the same rule. disagreement: product_id = 233 on the article (B only); dropped because nothing fixes it and the column is nullable. disagreement: form: A carries state = published as its own requirement, B folds it into the article; folded, with create_knowledge and create_knowledge (2) both named in source. disagreement: form: the link-removal sql (A adds case_id = 504, B the id alone); kept B's as the stricter test. disagreement: form: the stay on link 217 (A empty cells, B repeated columns); kept the row key as selector and the tested columns as cells. Several benchmark queries are not counts (SELECT assigned_to, SELECT state, SELECT reopen_count, SELECT location_id, SELECT sys_updated_on IS NOT NULL); the requirements restate them as COUNT(*) with the same substance. The benchmark's checks take the current user to be Tabitha Bullock (3): owner_id 3 and Liam's location 3 follow from that, while input.json names Kurt Fritz (96, a manager, allowed to reassign and reprioritise; user and membership creation fall under the policy's default admin role); the file follows input.json, with the benchmark's assumption recorded as evidence. The escalation flag is not required ('route it to the Escalation Management group' names the group; the policy's escalation rule is permissive). The entitlement verification passes on the seed (account-wide enterprise entitlements 213 and 216 cover product 233 under the policy's account-wide clause; 217 is the product's own standard one), so it is a read with no requirement. The request's premise that a current assigned user is blocked is false on the seed (assigned_to is null); nothing follows from it. The case's contact is 44, not Sabrina Buckley (contact 42); the request does not ask to change it. Retiring article 346 is not required: no tool does it and the request speaks of the link.
